items.title: P1Harmony Earns First No. 1 on Top Album Sales Chart With ‘BLOW UP’
items.summary:
P1Harmony earns its first No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Album Sales chart as BLOW UP bows atop the chart dated Nov. 21. It’s the seventh top 10-charted set for the pop group, which had previously topped out at No. 2, twice, with EX in 2025 and UNIQUE earlier in 2026.

BLOW UP begins with 43,000 copies sold in the United States in the week ending Nov. 12, according to Luminate. The set’s first-week sales were powered by its availability across 25 CD variants and five vinyl variants (all containing collectible items such as photocards and posters, with some items randomized).

Elsewhere in the top 10 of the latest Top Album Sales chart, Kings of Leon and Steven Wilson debut, while Vince Guaraldi Trio’s classic soundtrack to A Charlie Brown Christmas returns. Plus, Ariana Grande’s Christmas & Chill reaches the top 10 for the first time after a new vinyl variant was released.

Kings of Leon clock its seventh top 10 on Top Album Sales with the No. 6 debut of O My Beloved , selling 11,000 copies. Steven Wilson collects his second top 10 as Requiem for a Village arrives at No. 9 with 8,000 sold.

A pair of seasonal albums are in the top 10, as the A Charlie Brown Christmas soundtrack climbs 13-8 with 9,000 sold (up 48%) and Grande’s Christmas & Chill re-enters at No. 10 with 7,000 sold (up 1,451%) after it a new Target-exclusive vinyl variant was released.

Billboard ’s Top Album Sales chart ranks the top-selling albums of the week based only on pure album sales (physical and digital download purchases combined). The chart’s history dates to May 25, 1991, the first week Billboard…
items.t: P1Harmony Earns First No. 1 on Top Album Sales Chart With ‘BLOW UP’

items.title: Darren Hayes Launches the 2026 ARIA Awards With Savage Garden’s ‘Affirmation’: Watch
items.summary:
Savage Garden is, sadly, long gone. But when Darren Hayes took the stage at the 2026 ARIA Awards on Wednesday night (Nov. 18) in Sydney, he reminded everyone tuned in exactly what they were missing.

Hayes got the 40 th anniversary ARIAs broadcast underway — and the emotions stirring — with a performance of “Affirmation,” the title track from Savage Garden’s second and final album from 1999.

It was both a surprise for guests, and a proper highlight, its lyrics resonating just as they did on release more than a quarter century ago. 

Hayes wasn’t done there. He returned to the ARIAs stage to present Tame Impala  spearhead Kevin Parker with the ARIA Global Impact Award, in recognition of his extraordinary international success and cultural impact in the past year.

For Hayes and his ex-Savage Garden bandmate Daniel Jones, the ARIA Awards is a warm and fuzzy place. At the 1997 edition, the pop group dominated with a then-record 10 wins, including album of the year and group of the year.

Savage Garden would collect a total of 14 career ARIAs, including the best-selling album award in 2000 for Affirmation , before disbanding in 2001.

The Brisbane group flew the flag high during their active years, and became one of a select handful of Australian groups to enjoy a No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Indeed, they did it twice: with 1998’s “Truly Madly Deeply,” and again in 2000 with “I Knew I Loved You,” while their 1997 track “I Want You” also entered the top 5 (peaking at No. 4). Both albums ( Savage Garden at No. 3, Affirmation at No. 6) cracked the top 10 of the Billboard 200.…
items.t: Darren Hayes Launches the 2026 ARIA Awards With Savage Garden’s ‘Affirmation’: Watch

items.title: The Deals: Yamaha Acquires Visual Technology Company Disguise for $280 Million & More
items.summary:
Yamaha Corporation , the musical instruments and audio products company, acquired Disguise , which provides visual technology for live events, location-based experiences and virtual production spanning software, hardware and creative and technical services. A public notice published by Yamaha on Friday (Nov. 13) pegs the price of the transaction at 215 million pounds ($281 million).

According to a press release, Disguise technology has powered the visuals for tours by Beyoncé, Taylor Swift and Bad Bunny, along with locations including the Burj Khalifa in Dubai and the Stade de France in Paris.

“Welcoming Disguise marks a major step for Yamaha as we move beyond the traditional boundaries of musical instruments and audio equipment to create new experiential value centred on sound and music,” Atsugi Yamaha , president/representative executive officer of Yamaha Corporation, said in a statement. “As part of our long-term growth strategy, we are expanding our audio business into adjacent areas, including entertainment. We will combine the strengths of Disguise and Yamaha while respecting the brand, technology, and global relationships Disguise has built with customers and partners. Together, we will make new waves in live entertainment.”

Following the acquisition, the Disguise “brand, identity and relationships with customers and partners will be preserved,” according to a press release, with Disguise becoming “a new pillar alongside Yamaha’s existing business.” — Chris Eggertsen

items.title: Bruno Mars Mourns Death of Father Peter Hernandez: ‘The Man That Taught Me Everything I Know’
items.summary:
Bruno Mars has announced that his father, Peter Hernandez, passed away. The Grammy-winning superstar broke the tragic news with a heartbreaking tribute post to Instagram on Thursday (Nov. 19), mourning the loss of his dad. 

Related 

Stevie Wonder Says It’s ‘Bulls—‘ to Call Bruno Mars an Appropriator 

Bruno Mars Says He Has ‘Only Love’ for Taylor Swift After Fans Accuse Him of Dissing Her 

Bruno Mars’ ‘The Romantic’: All 9 Tracks Ranked 

“Last week I got to hug my father one last time,” Mars began. “If you’ve ever seen me talk about him I’ve always said that he’s the man that taught me everything I know, especially when it comes to music. He raised my four beautiful sisters, my brother, and me. 

The “I Just Might” singer continued: “In my eyes he was the greatest dad in the world, and I will miss him everyday until we meet again. I Love you Pops. Kiss mom up there for me.”

The 41-year-old included a hospital photo with his late father, while also posting several throwback pictures of his musically-inclined dad. Details of Hernandez’s death remain scarce. He was 74 years old. 

Mars lost his mother, Bernadette San Pedro Bayot, back in 2013 to a brain aneurysm. Bayot and Hernandez got divorced when the singer was about 12 years old in the mid-to-late ’90s, which led to a split of the family’s The Love Notes band. 

“My whole sense of rhythm is because my dad was teaching me bongos as a kid. He’s an old-school working musician, so that’s where the pinky rings come from, the patent-leather shoes, the suits, and the pompadour. It all stems from watching my father,” Mars…

items.title: Molly Santana Pushes Back at ‘Queen of the Underground’ Title: ‘The Underground Doesn’t Really Like Women’
items.summary:
Don’t call Molly Santana “The Queen of the Underground.”

The West Coast rapper recently sat down with Bootleg Kev to promote her upcoming album Black Punk and pushed back when Kev referred to her as “The Queen of the Underground.”

“I don’t want to be queen of the underground,” she said before expressing that she feels like that particular scene isn’t exactly welcoming to women. “They’re mean… Bro, it’s rough. They spot that I be in, it’s rough. Not to be like so negative, but the underground doesn’t really like women. But we already knew that.”

“It’s such a love/hate relationship,” Santana continued.

Elsewhere in the interview, she talked about being featured on Iceman’s “Ran to Atlanta” with Drake and Future and was asked who she was “more stoked” to be on the song with. “Equally geeked up, bro,” she said. “The thing is, bro, both speak to my soul. What do you mean? Those are my f—kin’ GOATS, bruh. You pull up songs from them and I will sing them with my whole spirit and head and toes, screaming.

Adding, “I just appreciate the performance art. Both of them have devoted their life to what they do, and that’s real. That’s some real popstar s—t.”

When talking with The Cruz Show  at Real 92.3 L.A. , she admitted to liking her verse on “Ran to Atlanta” at first, saying that she recorded her verse “maybe like five times, six times” and didn’t want Drake and his team to pick the version that made the album.

items.title: Summer Walker’s Interscope Lawsuit Heats Up as Star Accuses Label of Misusing Her IP

As Summer Walker and Interscope Records continue to hash out a contract dispute, the R&B singer is now accusing the Universal Music Group (UMG) label of wrongly monetizing her intellectual property.  

Walker’s countersuit, submitted to Los Angeles court on Wednesday (Nov. 18) and reviewed by Billboard , comes a month after Interscope sued her for $50 million over the terms of their 2017 record deal. The document formalizes Walker’s assertion that the record deal is now void under California’s seven-year limit on personal services contracts. 

Related 

Summer Walker Can Break Her Record Deal. But There’s a $50 Million Catch. 

Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support — For Now — to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight

Additionally, Walker is leveling up the dispute with new breach of contract and unjust enrichment claims. The singer alleges that Interscope has been using her intellectual property beyond the bounds of the record deal, which solely granted rights for the label to exploit and promote her music.

Walker alleges that she personally retains ownership of all her other IP, including the content she posts to social media. But according to Walker, Interscope has been reposting her digital content on YouTube and other platforms — and making money from it.

items.title: Chucho Valdés Turns 85 & Keeps Rocking His 88 Keys
items.summary:
Chucho Valdés celebrated his 85th birthday on Oct. 9 with a party at his house (replete with musicians, of course); with a series of concerts across the U.S. during which he played both solo and with an ensemble featuring  jazz notables like saxophonist  Joe Lovano , bassist  John Patitucci , drummer Marcus Gilmore and percussionist  Roberto Jr. Vizcaino Torre ; and with a solo album, UNCUT , released prior to his big day.

The album was a particularly oversized achievement for Valdés, a towering musical figure with a towering height (6-foot-5) to match. UNCUT — released on indie InnerJazz (part of InnerCat Music, Valdés’ label since the early 2000s) — is an eight-track set recorded completely live by Valdés on his favorite Steinway grand, with no cuts, no edits and no second takes. It’s the kind of exercise in musicianship, inspiration and joy that’s allowed Valdés to remain an essential figure in both the jazz and Latin music worlds; a man whose music spans countries, generations and genres.

Reaching back to his origins as the son of another legendary pianist, Bebo Valdés, Chucho has traversed the musical world from classical to experimental jazz, famously creating Cuban experimental group Irakere alongside Paquito D’Rivera and Arturo Sandoval, then launching into other realms with abandon, collecting seven Grammys and seven Latin Grammys along the way.

“Imagine. The piano is the soundtrack of my entire life. I was born listening to it and then I learned it,” says Valdés today.

In celebration of his monumental year and his 85th birthday, Valdés spoke with Billboard .…
items.t: Chucho Valdés Turns 85 & Keeps Rocking His 88 Keys

items.title: Chvrches share tongue-in-cheek new single ‘Evil’ and announce UK album launch shows in churches
items.summary:
Chvrches have shared another new single, ‘Evil’, and announced some special album launch shows – taking place in UK churches. Listen and find all the details below.

The song is the third preview of the Scottish trio’s fifth studio album, ‘All The King’s Men’ , which is released on January 22.

READ MORE:  How trauma and friendship launched new Chvrches project The Leaving: “This was always supposed to happen” 

Following on from ‘Overthinker’ and ‘Roses’ , the latest track from Lauren Mayberry and co. is described as a “sharp, modern feminist anthem”. It takes inspiration from psychedelic folk while blending guitars, a gospel-tinged chorus and eerie lyrics.

“ They say I’ve a madness, that I’m rotten to the core/ So how come every night I’m singing, everybody screams for more? ” the frontwoman asks. “ Evil, I’ll be everything you need/ Evil, I’ll leave you crawling on your knees/ Evil, I’ll have you begging, ‘Baby, please’/ Evil, I’ll leave you crawling on your knees .”

As for how the single came about, Mayberry explained: “I struggled for a long time with feeling misread when it came to talking about issues that seemed fairly straightforward and like common sense to me. It was confusing, in my early 20s, to feel cast as this ‘vicious woman’ I didn’t identify with and to receive that kind of vitriol, but that was a very fun character to channel when writing this song.”

She continued: “Ironically, I wasn’t even that angry back then but I probably am now, and I’m OK with that. I DO feel angry sometimes – I don’t know how any woman isn’t, in this moment in time, and I…

items.title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ review: David Fincher cuts loose with Tarantino’s ’70s hangout sequel
items.summary:
C liff fucking Booth. That’s Quentin Tarantino’s stuntman character. You know, the one played by Brad Pitt, the sidekick-driver-buddy of Leonardo DiCaprio ’s fading TV star Rick Dalton from his masterpiece Once Upon A Time.. In Hollywood , way back in 2019. Cliff Booth, the one who had to remind his panicky, tormented boss, in that signature California drawl, that he’s Rick fucking Dalton.

Read more: The best films of 2026… so far! 

David Fincher is behind the wheel of this sequel, directing the Tarantino script, in an odd-couple auteur collaboration that glides then crunches, glides then crunches. Maybe OUATIH ’s high-grade nostalgia isn’t quite as potent on the second hit, but who cares? It’s possible that no movie has ever vibed quite as hard as this movie vibes.

A neo-noirish shaggy dog story, it’s set in a 1977 Los Angeles – eight years after Rick and Cliff “subdued” some hippies – to a car-radio soundtrack of disco classics, soul deep cuts and a mostly low-key, jazzy score from Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross. The romance of the radio call-in requests alone makes the whole damn internet age seem cheap, stale and sterile. And if you see this film in IMAX, you’ll want to climb into the screen. The burger joint lights, the New Beverly Cinema, the RC Cola – all served by the swoon-worthy cinematography. You can almost smell the city.

Brad Pitt in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’. CREDIT: Netflix 
 It’s really not about the plot, which sees Cliff bouncing between projectionist, bartending and fixer jobs before getting mixed up with Hollywood agent Karen…

items.title: Beabadoobee announces surprise new album ‘Bananas 4 Cats’ with sweet single ‘No Punctuation’
items.summary:
Beabadoobee has announced a surprise new album, ‘Bananas 4 Cats’ – listen to the single ‘No Punctuation’ below.

READ MORE: Beabadoobee live in London: Four albums in, she’s reached arena headline status her own way 

The singer-songwriter is due to release her fifth studio record on February 19 via Dirty Hit/Interscope. It’ll come just five months after she dropped her previous LP, ‘Pylon’ , in September.

She teased the title of the forthcoming album during her headline show at London’s O2 last night (Wednesday November 18). Bea Laus also previewed ‘No Punctuation’ in the encore, telling fans that it would be out today (Thursday November 19).

The track is a gentle, acoustic guitar-driven number on which she sweetly sings about her partner: “ ‘Cause you are everything .” ‘No Punctuation’ dates back more than four years, with early versions previously appearing online.

View this post on Instagram 

Laus has been road-testing the single at recent UK gigs on her current ‘Powerlines’ tour .

Explaining how ‘Bananas 4 Cats’ came together, she explained: “I just needed to write an album like this after ‘Pylon’. It happened naturally; I got back home and felt inspired, and made another album.”

According to a press release, the “overriding theme” of Laus’ next LP is “home”. It adds: “Whereas its predecessor was written, recorded and about being on the road, with an extensive cast of collaborators, the new album was written and recorded in east London, in Bea’s living room, with just her friend, her partner and her cats.”

The tracklist for Beabadoobee’s ‘Bananas 4 Cats’ is yet…

The singer-songwriter’s new take on the Big Thief frontwoman’s 2020 solo song is the latest entry into her ever-growing Christmas catalogue. Proceeds from the track from both Bridgers and Lenker will benefit the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund (PCRF).

Bridgers’ cosy and intimate version remains faithful to the original, as she sings about spending the holidays with family: “ Christmas Eve with your mother and sis/ Don’t wanna fight, but your mother insists/ Dog’s white teeth slice right through my fist/ Drive to the ER and they put me on risk .”

The cover was produced by Bridgers alongside her longtime collaborators Tony Berg and Ethan Gruska, as well as Jack Antonoff . All three are credited as producers on her third album ‘Lost Weekend’ , which was released in August.

Bridgers has previously marked the festive period with covers of Tom Waits’ ‘Day After Tomorrow’ , yuletide classic ‘Have Yourself A Merry Little Christmas’, Merle Haggard’s ‘If We Make It Through December’ , Simon & Garfunkel’s ‘7 O’Clock News/Silent Night’ (with Fiona Apple and The National’s Matt Berninger) , and McCarthy Trenching’s ‘Christmas Song’ (with Jackson Browne) .

She then took on The Handsome Family’s ‘So Much Wine’ in 2022, with proceeds going to the Los Angeles LGBT Center .

items.title: Renegade country, Flash FM and true crime podcasts: your guide to the best ‘GTA 6’ radio stations
items.summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is twice as big as the already-huge open world of GTA 5 and, according to the reviews and early impressions , it’s a lot more detailed too.

What this means is you’re going to have a lot of ground to cover as you take former soldier Jason Duval and ex-con Lucia Caminos through the streets of Vice City.

READ MORE: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ review: one of the best games ever made 

“When an easy score goes wrong, [Jason and Lucia] find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida,” reads an official description of the game’s story, “forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.” It sounds like we’re in for one hell of a ride.

And you’re going to want the perfect soundtrack to go with that compelling adventure. Luckily, Justice have created an original score with plenty of groovy synths and disco swagger that sets the mood for the lawless neon playground – but you can also pick your own music via one of Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s 22 in-game radio stations. In previous titles, you had to be in a vehicle to access the carefully-curated mixes presented by celebrity hosts. Thanks to the addition of smartphones and earbuds in GTA 6 though, you’re now free to take the music with you wherever you roam. Here are our favourite stations – and when and why you should be tuning into them:

Cocoteo FM 
 Hosted by : El Martillo and La Gata (Bad Bunny and RaiNao)

She keeps her collection of T-shirts, posters, vinyl and other merch celebrating the late singer-songwriter in what she affectionately calls her “Buckley box”. items.title: Trance, prog synths, guttural screaming: Lorenzo Senni’s All Ages is the year’s wildest electronic album
items.summary:
(Warp)
The Milan producer revisits his youth as a straight-edge punk fan voyeuristically dabbling in rave – and finds a thrilling interzone between both genres

The opening line of the biography on Lorenzo Senni’s Bandcamp page is striking. “Lorenzo Senni was never a raver,” it reads, something of a blunt admission from a dance producer, or at least a producer who works in an area of electronica influenced by dance music: one might reasonably assume you need some first-hand experience of the dancefloor’s ineffable freedom in order to make music for it. But the Milan-based Senni has made a USP out of his arm’s length distance from what that Bandcamp bio calls a “neon-hued chemical world”.

A straight-edge punk fan in the late 90s, he accompanied friends to Rimini’s hardcore and gabber clubs as a kind of anthropological exercise, a self-styled “rave voyeur” who “just liked to observe and analyse my surroundings”. Accordingly, his albums to date have dealt in what approving critics like to call deconstructions or interrogations of dance music rather than dance music itself: 2012’s Quantum Jelly and 2014’s Superimpositions featured what Senni called “pointillistic trance”, spinning the icy, staccato notes and arpeggiated synth lines of the genre’s epic breakdowns into lengthy, beatless tracks that never reached the climax implied. items.summary:
He was nearly an early rock’n’roll star but took a different path, from Fats Domino to the Band and pro-environment songwriting. As a career-spanning box set is released, those who knew him remember an American original

‘I was listening to Bob Dylan’s Theme Time radio show,” says Korey Richey, multi-instrumentalist with LCD Soundsystem, “and he said, ‘Bobby Charles is best known as a songwriter, but he has one of the most melodious voices ever transmuted into a piece of vinyl.’ I thought about it, and I agree: Bobby Charles was something else.”

Something else, indeed. Charles (1938–2010) was unable to play an instrument yet wrote songs sung by everyone from Fats Domino to Etta James to Kris Kristofferson. Signed to Chess Records in 1955 aged 17, he was on the verge of becoming a star at the dawn of rock’n’roll, but a preference for living reclusively – with a pet alligator – ensured he vanished from sight, and his music has long been unavailable. “He was a very strange guy, a loner,” says one of his Louisiana contemporaries, 88-year-old Johnnie Allan. “He knew what he had and wouldn’t compromise.” Now a box set, The Bobby Charles Story, containing almost every recording Charles released, aims to establish the Cajun magus as one of the greats.

items.title: They’re one of the UK’s greatest cult bands – who swore they’d never reunite. What brought Life Without Buildings back together?
items.summary:
The Scottish quartet existed for just three years at the turn of the millennium. But after Frank Ocean and TikTok thrilled to Sue Tompkins’ unique vocals, they’re back. They explain their fears about ‘spoiling the joy’

‘I’m excited, I’m scared, I’m anxious – that bubbling feeling, like when you’re on a rollercoaster, at the very top, just before the big drop.”

On a drizzly afternoon in July, huddled with her three bandmates in the cramped cupboard that’s the dressing room of Glasgow venue Mono, Sue Tompkins is managing her feelings ahead of her first proper gig with Life Without Buildings in almost a quarter of a century. “Everybody coming is invited, it’s secret, nobody paid much to get in, the profits are going to charity,” adds guitarist Robert Dallas Gray, sat beside her, as much to steady his own nerves as to explain the circumstances of tonight’s show. “I hope people aren’t looking at it like we’re fucking entertainers.”

items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote]

items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

items.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
items.summary:
Bristol Beacon
The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.
